name: Lafayette County, MS
findings: Lafayette County has 170 nonprofit organizations. 67 of them (39%) list at least one way to get involved on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 60 organizations.
Social and fraternal organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (37% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Lafayette County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.
27% of the organizations offering opportunities have no identified type, so the breakdown by type is partial.

observations.title: Fewer organizations list volunteering
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Lafayette County list volunteering on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 67% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 28 organizations here; 45% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find ways to volunteer now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Fewer organizations list public events
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Lafayette County list public events on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 70% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 50 organizations here; 45% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find public events now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Social and fraternal organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 10 social and fraternal organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity on their websites. Many may still offer them without saying so online, or have no website at all.

confidence.text: Based on 10 organizations here; 45% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What do social and fraternal organizations here do in the community? How do people find out about them?

observations.title: Few religious organizations list membership
observations.text: 3 religious organizations here list membership. In similar places of this size, about 9 would.

confidence.text: Based on 9 organizations here; 45% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Do people here look for groups to join through religious groups? Where else does that happen?
